subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & pricing — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & pricing — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before I run a detailed cost model: 

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Workload: conversational agent + summarization pipelines for customer support logs
- Expected steady-state: ~3M tokens/day (read + write combined)
- Peak concurrency: ~100–140 RPS (peaks during business hours)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for short-turn chat flows
- Model family: Llama-3-like (67B) or equivalent (you mentioned open-model preference)
- Data residency: US only; some data subject to strict retention rules for a regulated vertical

Deployment preferences you mentioned on the call:
- Primary: Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput
- Secondary: Private VPC/on-prem evaluation for regulated subsidiaries (if procurement requires)

What I need from you to run a tight cost model (I attached a small template):
1) Clarify average tokens per request (prompt + response). If you don’t know, give a representative example (e.g., 250 in, 550 out = 800 avg).
2) Expected monthly active days (do weekends see similar load?)
3) Whether you require on-prem (air-gapped) for all traffic or just a subset (e.g., regulated customers only).

High level guidance (so you have framing while we model):
- Hosted API: simplest to start; per-token billing, no infra management. Best for variable workloads and fast time-to-market.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): better unit economics for sustained high QPS; predictable monthly commit (reserved GPU pools) lowers per-token cost but requires a usage/commit estimate.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict compliance/air-gap. Higher up-front and ongoing ops costs (appliances, network/setup, support).

I’ve attached the redwood-deployment-pricing-template.xlsx — fill the avg tokens and monthly days and I’ll run two scenarios: Hosted per-token vs Dedicated reserved (3- and 6-month commit) and an order-of-magnitude Private runbook cost.

Proposed next steps:
- You fill in the two small fields in the sheet and reply with the file (or I can pre-fill from your numbers).
- I’ll produce a short two-page cost comparison and we can schedule a 30-min call with Dylan (solutions engineer) to review trade-offs and sizing.

If that sounds good I’ll block time for a review next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-deployment-pricing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & pricing — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — helps a lot. I filled the template and attached a procurement timeline. Key clarifications from our side: 
- Average tokens per conversational turn ~ 800 (we see 250 tokens in prompts, ~550 tokens generated across summarization + follow-ups).
- Monthly active days: 22 (weekdays primarily)
- For now we want Dedicated for our main product. We also need Private/VPC options scoped for one regulated vertical (about 10% of traffic) — potentially a separate deployment.

High-level constraints:
- Budget committee expects a clear per-month cost comparison: Hosted (per-token), Dedicated (monthly reserved), and estimate for Private (one-time + monthly ops).
- Procurement timeline: approvals by end of April. I attached the procurement_schedule.pdf.

Can you send a ballpark table that compares: cost/month for our expected profile (3M tokens/day, 22 days/mo, 800 avg tokens/request) for:
A) Hosted per-token
B) Dedicated reserved (3-month and 12-month commit scenarios)
C) Private (CAPEX and OPEX ballpark)

Happy to schedule the review with Dylan next week — available Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product | Acme Analytics
alex.rivera@acmeanalytics.com

Attachment: procurement_schedule.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & pricing — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Alex —

Thanks for the details and the procurement timeline — that’s very helpful. I ran a preliminary model (see assumptions below) and drafted ballpark monthly numbers so your finance and procurement teams have something to react to. I’ll produce a line-item sheet after you confirm the assumptions and we can review on Tue/Wed with Dylan.

Assumptions used: 
- Avg tokens/request = 800
- Daily tokens = 3M/day * 22 days = 66M tokens/month
- Model = 67B open model equivalent; inference performance consistent with Redwood profiles

Preliminary cost comparison (ballpark):
A) Hosted (per-token)
- Unit: $0.00065 per token (example hosted rate for 67B quality class)
- Monthly = 66,000,000 * $0.00065 = $42,900 / month

B) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — illustrative (sustained commit lowers unit cost)
- 3-month reserved pool (sized for your peak concurrency): estimated commit ~$32,000 / month -> effective unit ~$0.00048 per token -> ~$31,680 / month
- 12-month reserved commitment: estimated commit ~$27,000 / month -> effective unit ~$0.00041 per token -> ~$27,060 / month
- Notes: reserved pricing assumes autoscaling + burst allowance; we’d size GPUs for peak concurrency and operations overhead included in commit.

C) Private (VPC / on-prem) — order of magnitude
- One-time setup (appliance + network + integration): $120k–$220k depending on on-prem requirements
- Monthly O&M + support: $8k–$18k / month (plus any infra leases) -> effective unit varies widely but likely comparable to dedicated if fully utilized.

Key caveats & inputs needed to refine:
- Actual GPU topology we pick (A100 vs H100 vs local inference boxes) changes commit sizing.
- Concurrency profile across 24h vs burst windows (if traffic is heavily spiky, dedicated sizing might need higher commit).
- Whether regulated subset requires separate private footprint; if it’s only ~10% of traffic we can model hybrid (Dedicated for 90% + Private for 10%).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the avg tokens and days (you already did; I used your numbers).
2) I’ll produce a downloadable comparison spreadsheet with line-item math and a recommended commit (3-month vs 12-month) so procurement can see the discount curve.
3) Schedule a 30-min review with Dylan next Tue/Wed afternoon PT — I’ve tentatively penciled 2026-03-10 2:00 PM PT.

Would you like us to include a sample service-level appendix (latency SLOs, incident response, data handling) for the procurement packet? We can include a private-deployment checklist if you want to start that conversation in parallel.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: architecture-diagram.pdf

We’re fine to proceed with the Tue 2:00 PM PT review — Sophie and I will join; procurement will be on the invite as needed. After that call we’ll ask legal for a standard terms sheet.
